sources.researchNote: A text-only listing, without a picture, among the hotels the paper recommended in Paris. It reads: “Le Home aristocratique par excellence, dont le cadre et l’atmosphère procureront à chacun la délicieuse sensation du « chez soi »”. The hotel presented itself as a residential hotel for longer stays, which fits Kaper’s giving it as his home address in 1934.

places.publicNote: Kaper gave this Paris hotel as his home address on the S.S. Champlain passenger manifest before arriving in New York. It was a hotel address rather than a private residence: in 1931 the Château Frontenac advertised itself as an aristocratic “home” that would give guests the feeling of being “chez soi”, that is, as a residential hotel for longer stays.
